newsitem.title: USA: Ray lawyers want to test-fire rifle again-report.
newsitem.headline: Ray lawyers want to test-fire rifle again-report.

text.p: Lawyers for James Earl Ray want to conduct additional tests on the rifle he supposedly used to assassinate civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr., a newspaper said Wednesday.

The Memphis Commercial Appeal cited an affidavit from a firearms expert the lawyers hired to test the hunting rifle. The lawyers argued the inside of the rifle barrel should have been cleaned with a bronze brush before test-firing, but the firearms expert said he thought the judge wanted the rifle fired without cleaning.

Experts compared test bullets fired from the rifle with the bullet that killed King using an electron microscope at a Pennsylvania laboratory. The results of that comparison were scheduled to be aired in a Memphis court June 18.

If the rifle were ruled out as the murder weapon, that could open the way for a trial for Ray, who pleaded guilty to killing King and received a 99-year sentence. Two days after pleading guilty, Ray recanted and he has sought a trial ever since, a position supported by King's family.
Two previous tests by government examiners in 1968, the year of the killing, and 1978 failed to prove conclusively whether the fatal bullet came from Ray's rifle.

Earlier this week, Ray, who is 69 and dying from liver failure, lost an appeal asking that he be allowed to travel to Pittsburgh for tests on whether he would be a suitable candidate to receive a liver transplant.
